Role of APIbase APIbase is a technology intermediary; buyer funds do not pass through APIbase; the fee is charged to the merchant. APIbase is operated by its operator, an individual independent open-source developer (the "Operator"), identified by the domain apibase.pro, the public repository github.com/whiteknightonhorse/APIbase and the address support@apibase.pro. There is no registered company. "APIbase" in these documents means the Operator. The Operator may transfer this role to a company or a successor operator of apibase.pro with 30 days' notice at /legal. APIbase is not the seller, is not a payment institution, and does not hold funds. The buyer pays USDC directly to the merchant's wallet. APIbase provides the storefront, the quote, the order record and the notifications. Notices to APIbase go to support@apibase.pro. Notices to the merchant go to the contact e-mail in the merchant profile; the merchant keeps it current. 2. Fee and settlement Fee: 0% during the pilot, minimum $0.05 per order, charged to the merchant. Tempo (MPP): the fee is taken in the buyer's transaction as a split; the merchant receives the order total minus the fee. Base (x402): the fee is taken in the same transaction when the buyer's client supports fee-split; otherwise it is not part of the transaction and APIbase invoices it to the merchant, payable in USDC. Pilot: the fee is 0%. The Fee Switch can change this only under section 9. 3. Merchant obligations Goods and services offered are lawful in the merchant's country and in the buyer's country. Returns follow the law of the merchant's country and the published refund policy (see Refund Framework). The merchant issues closing documents (invoices, receipts) to the buyer. The merchant is responsible for its own taxes, including any VAT or sales tax on its orders. The merchant answers order disputes within 7 days. The merchant confirms a paid order within 48 hours (SLA). If an order is duplicated through APIbase's fault, the refund is made within 7 days. The merchant alone is responsible for its products: product safety, warranty, consumer-law compliance, delivery and after-sales service. The merchant grants APIbase a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to show its catalog, product texts, images and prices on the storefront, in agent-readable files and in discovery indexes, for as long as the storefront is active, and warrants that it holds the rights to that content. The merchant represents that neither it, its owners nor its payout wallets are on a sanctions list (including the OFAC SDN list) and that it is not registered in a country listed in the Acceptable Use Policy section 4. 4. Suspension and termination APIbase may suspend or disconnect a merchant that breaks this Agreement or the Acceptable Use Policy, with immediate effect for prohibited goods, fraud, sanctions matches or a lawful request. Either party may end this Agreement for convenience with 30 days' notice. The merchant may deactivate its storefront at any time; open orders remain to be served. Sections 3, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14 and 15 survive termination. 5. Reputation APIbase may show order statistics and dispute outcomes for a merchant on its storefront. 6. Changes APIbase publishes a new version of these documents at /legal with its version, effective date and hash. A new version takes effect 30 days after it is posted, except changes required by law, changes that only add tools or lower prices, and corrections of errors, which take effect on posting. The merchant is notified at the contact e-mail of its profile and in API responses ( terms_update_pending ). The merchant accepts the new version by signing the new document hashes; once the version is in effect, new quotes are refused until it is accepted. 7. Liability APIbase's liability to the merchant is limited to the greater of the fees received from that merchant in the previous 12 months and USD 100. Neither party is liable for indirect or consequential loss, lost profit, lost data or lost business, except for fraud, wilful misconduct or where the law does not allow this exclusion. 8. No warranty; blockchains and payment rails The storefront, the quotes, the notifications and the APIbase software are provided "as is" and "as available", without warranty of any kind, including fitness for a particular purpose and uninterrupted operation. APIbase does not operate the Base or Tempo networks, the USDC token, wallets, facilitators or settlers, and is not liable for their outages, fees (gas), delays, chain reorganisations, lost keys or transactions sent to a wrong address. On-chain transactions are irreversible; a payment is treated as made when the network confirms it. 9. Fee Switch The fee may be switched on or off by APIbase with 30 days' notice at the contact e-mail of the merchant profile. The current state is shown at /pricing. 10. Subscriptions and streams A subscription product states its price per period, the period length, the renewal window and the grace period on its storefront page before the buyer subscribes. Renewal is charged only inside the renewal window, only for the stated amount, and only against an authorisation the buyer's agent signed; the merchant never charges beyond it. The buyer can cancel at any time; cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid period and no further charge is made. An unpaid renewal moves the subscription to past_due and then ends it; nothing is charged retroactively. A stream product states its rate per second and the minimum deposit before the buyer opens it. The buyer may close the stream at any time; only consumed seconds are settled to the merchant and the unconsumed deposit is returned through the payment channel. Consumed seconds are refundable only under the merchant's published refund policy. A product sold this way is not a "negative option" under the Acceptable Use Policy when it meets this section. 11. Orders placed by agents The merchant accepts orders placed by autonomous software agents. An order placed by an agent binds the principal the agent acts for; the merchant may rely on the quote, the payment and the delivery data as received. Refunds of an order placed by mistake follow the merchant's published refund policy. 12. Indemnity The merchant indemnifies APIbase against third-party claims, fines and reasonable costs arising from the merchant's goods, content, taxes, data handling or breach of these documents. 13. Compliance APIbase may at any time refuse a quote, suspend the storefront, withhold a fee split or invoice credit, and report to authorities where sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering rules or a lawful request require it. APIbase holds no merchant funds and therefore cannot freeze funds already paid to the merchant. 14. General Neither party is liable for delay caused by events outside its reasonable control (force majeure). If a clause is unenforceable the rest stays in force. These documents are the entire agreement on their subject. The merchant may not assign this Agreement without APIbase's consent; APIbase may assign it to a successor operator of apibase.pro with notice. 15. Governing law and disputes These documents are governed by the law of England and Wales, without regard to its conflict-of-law rules; mandatory consumer or data-protection rules of your country still apply where they cannot be excluded. A dispute is first negotiated in good faith for 30 days from written notice. Any dispute not resolved in that period shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration under the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules before a single arbitrator, conducted online in English, seat London; either party may instead bring a claim in the small-claims court of its own country for amounts within that court's limit. Claims are brought individually, not as a class or representative action, where the applicable law allows this waiver. Terms · Privacy · Contact · Legal · GitHub
